bull.b: The rapidly expanding backlog provides stronger multi-quarter revenue visibility across both launch and Space Systems. Its balanced composition reduces reliance on a single offering, while the expected conversion of nearly one-third within 12 months supports sustained growth.

A long operating record and improving production cadence strengthen Rocket Lab’s credibility with commercial and government customers. Reliable execution can support repeat awards, higher utilization, and a durable competitive position as launch demand expands.

Substantial liquidity and conservative leverage give Rocket Lab financial flexibility to fund Neutron, production expansion, and strategic initiatives without immediate solvency pressure. This balance-sheet capacity supports execution through a capital-intensive growth phase.

bear.b: Rocket Lab has not yet converted revenue growth into sustainable profitability or self-funded cash generation. Continued operating and investment burn can consume liquidity, constrain capital allocation, and increase dependence on future financing while the business scales.

The delay postpones Rocket Lab’s entry into medium-lift launch and extends the period of elevated development spending before the program can contribute commercially. Further testing or production issues could defer the expected improvement in earnings and cash flow.

Funding a major acquisition through substantial share issuance can dilute existing ownership and increase the execution burden of integrating Iridium. The transaction must generate durable strategic and cash-flow benefits to offset the enlarged equity base.
